notes: Round 58. All nine are supreme-audit-institution or parliamentary-inquiry findings, the shape already filed for Guyana and Belize.

records.people: Accountant General of Barbados (unnamed); Auditor General of Barbados (unnamed)
records.summary: The Auditor General's 2004 report found discrepancies between the Accountant General's records and the records of the Central Bank of Barbados for the government current account, arising between October 2000 and February 2004. Withdrawals not recorded by the Accountant General exceeded $1.8 million and unrecorded deposits exceeded $6.8 million, including a $4.48 million transaction the Auditor General had already said in 2003 warranted investigation.
records.source_title: Report of the Auditor General for the year 2004 (Barbados Audit Office)
records.quote: withdrawals not recorded by the Accountant General which are in excess of $1.8 million and deposits not recorded which are in excess of $6.8

records.summary: The Auditor General's 2020 report found that bank reconciliations for Treasury accounts at the Central Bank of Barbados were not completed up to 31 March 2019, and that the Central Bank account had last been reconciled in May 2018. The report noted that monthly reconciliation is an internal control that can detect fraud or errors.
records.source_title: Report of the Auditor General for the year 2020 (Barbados Audit Office)
records.quote: the Central Bank account was last reconciled in May 2018

records.people: Government of Barbados (Treasury); Auditor General of Barbados (unnamed)
records.summary: The Auditor General's 2020 report found that the government's overdraft facility at the Central Bank of Barbados exceeded its statutory limit of 10 per cent of estimated revenue ($323.303 million) twice between 1 April 2018 and 31 July 2018, each time by $10 million, contrary to the legislation.
records.source_title: Report of the Auditor General for the year 2020 (Barbados Audit Office)
records.quote: The Overdraft facility at the Central Bank exceeded its limit of 10% of estimated revenue ($323.303 million twice between the 1st April 2018

records.summary: The Auditor General's 2020 report examined 29 transactions in which the Accountant General authorises the Central Bank of Barbados by signed memorandum to transfer loan funds to lending agencies. Eight transfers totalling $13.137 million had no supporting memorandum, which the report called a breach of controls that increases the risk of unauthorised payments.
records.source_title: Report of the Auditor General for the year 2020 (Barbados Audit Office)
records.quote: eight (8) totaling $13.137 million were not. This shows a breach of controls and increases the risk of unauthorized payments occurring.

records.summary: The Auditor General's 2021 report found that cheques totalling $10,198,548.08 recorded on Treasury cashiers' reports for 22 September 2020 did not agree with the Central Bank of Barbados listing, which recorded $3,536,006.77, a difference of $6,662,541.31 for which no explanation was given. The same report found interest charges of $840,926.31 on the Treasury overdraft account at the Central Bank for August and November 2020 appeared on Central Bank statements but were not entered in the government ledger.
records.source_title: Report of the Auditor General for the year 2021 (Barbados Audit Office)
records.quote: did not agree to the Central Bank Listing which recorded $3,536,006.77 resulting in a difference of $6,662,541.31. No explanation was presented

records.summary: In its report and opinion on the 2019 General State Account, Timor-Leste's Court of Accounts found that 6.6 million US dollars of European Union direct budget support, held in three bank accounts at the Banco Central de Timor-Leste, was not booked as state revenue, so 2019 state revenue was understated by that amount, and the 2.3 million US dollars spent from those accounts was spent outside the state budget and the General State Account. The report also recorded a closing accounting balance of 4.4 million US dollars against a cash balance at the central bank of 5.2 million US dollars.
records.source_title: Relatorio e Parecer sobre a Conta Geral do Estado 2019 (Tribunal de Recurso, Camara de Contas)
records.quote: O valor de 6,6 milhoes USD constitui receita do Estado do ano de 2019 e por esta razao deveria ter sido contabilizada

parties.party: Camara de Contas, Tribunal de Recurso de Timor-Leste
parties.name_as_stated: TRIBUNAL DE RECURSO CAMARA DE CONTAS

records.summary: Aruba's General Audit Chamber, reviewing the country's 2001-2004 annual accounts, found that contributions paid into an earmarked account held at the Centrale Bank van Aruba in the country's name for the Fondo Desaroyo Aruba foundation were not accounted for completely, correctly and on time. Of a balance of 19.3 million Aruban florins at the end of 2000, only the 3 million paid in by Aruba appeared in the country's accounts, while 16,898,503 florins paid in by the Netherlands were left off the balance sheet.
records.source_title: Onderzoek naar de jaarrekeningen Land 2001-2004 (Algemene Rekenkamer Aruba)
records.quote: werden niet volledig, juist en tijdig verantwoord

records.people: Ikililou Dhoinine (President of the Union of the Comoros)
records.summary: The Comorian parliament's commission of inquiry into the economic citizenship programme reported in December 2017 that, according to his own collaborators, President Ikililou Dhoinine ordered that from January 2015 until the end of his term the programme's funds no longer be paid into the Banque Centrale des Comores, and that he could not explain what became of them. The commission concluded that he was therefore suspected of embezzling public money.
records.source_title: Rapport de la Commission d'enquete parlementaire sur la loi relative a la citoyennete economique (Assemblee de l'Union des Comores)
records.quote: ordonne de ne plus verser les fonds de la citoyennete economique a la banque centrale de janvier 2015 a la fin de son

parties.party: Assemblee de l'Union des Comores, Commission d'enquete parlementaire
parties.name_as_stated: Commission d'Enquete parlementaire creee au sein de l'Assemblee de l'Union

records.people: Banque Centrale des Comores Board of Directors (unnamed); Mze Abdou Mohamed Chanfiou (former BCC governor)
records.summary: The same parliamentary inquiry recorded that the economic citizenship account TR0044 held at the Banque Centrale des Comores received payments, including four cheques drawn by Comoro Gulf Holding on two commercial banks between March 2009 and April 2010, and that the central bank booked money into the account without knowing the price at which the passports were being sold. The bank's board noted in June 2014 that 6 million euros had been expected before the end of December 2013 while receipts since October 2013 came to only 2.670 million Comorian francs, which the inquiry called a shortfall of more than 2,900,000,000 Comorian francs. The account was closed on 1 September 2015.
records.source_title: Rapport de la Commission d'enquete parlementaire sur la loi relative a la citoyennete economique (Assemblee de l'Union des Comores)
records.quote: La BCC enregistrait des entrees de fonds dans le compte de la citoyennete economique sans connaitre le prix auquel etait vendu le passeport.

parties.party: Assemblee de l'Union des Comores, Commission d'enquete parlementaire
